quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person who is 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person who is 21 or older is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.
Does not guarantee that the other driver will yield to you.
Means the other driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee that the other driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means another driver will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees absorb some of the impact. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Increase your speed to exit the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is usually on the right handlegrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before riding.

questions.question: When securing a load, you should place it:

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. Placing them high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and hurts balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the motorcycle to one side.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight and increases the braking force needed. Slowing and stopping take longer when going downhill with a sidecar.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact.
An inner liner that absorbs impact.
A chinstrap to keep it on.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.

questions.explanation: Before getting on a motorcycle, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When being passed, all of the following are potential hazards, except:

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that passengers may throw.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face in a crash.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.
